name: ADUM1400BRWZ-RL
title: ADuM1400/ADuM1401/ADuM1402: quad-channel digital isolators, 2500 V rms, up to 90 Mbps, 16-lead SOIC_W
summary: Four-channel digital isolators that pass logic signals across a 2500 V rms barrier through on-chip transformers. The ADuM1400 has all four channels running one way, the ADuM1401 three one way and one back, the ADuM1402 two each way; each side has an output-enable pin where it has outputs. Either side runs from 2.7 V to 5.5 V, so the part also translates between 3 V and 5 V logic. Grades A, B and C reach 1, 10 and 90 Mbps; the automotive WS and WT grades run to 125 °C. A refresh scheme keeps the outputs correct at DC and sets a known output state when the input side loses power.
key_figures: 27 ns typ, 32 ns max (C grade, 5 V)
1.0 mA per channel max at 0 to 2 Mbps; 3.5 mA at 10 Mbps; 31 mA at 90 Mbps
0.7 mA per channel max at 0 to 2 Mbps; 2.1 mA at 10 Mbps; 20 mA at 90 Mbps
2.7 V to 5.5 V each side (3.0 V to 5.5 V for W grades)
2500 V rms for 1 minute (UL 1577); VIORM 560 V peak

notes: Z marks a RoHS-compliant part and W a part qualified for automotive use.
Adding -RL to a model number orders it on a 13-inch reel of 1,000 units (ADUM1400BRWZ-RL is the ADuM1400BRWZ on such a reel). The ADuM1402BRW has no reel option.
EVAL-ADuMQSEBZ is the evaluation board for the family.

circuits.title: Recommended PCB layout and bypassing
circuits.description: The ADuM1400 with the only parts it needs: one bypass capacitor per side. C1 sits across VDD1 and GND1 at pins 1 and 2, C2 across VDD2 and GND2 at pins 16 and 15. The logic inputs and outputs and the enable run straight out to the circuits on each side with nothing between. On the ADuM1401 and ADuM1402 the same footprint carries the channels and enables of those pinouts.
notes: Pins 2 and 8 are one node inside the part, as are pins 9 and 15; both pins of each pair go to that side's ground.
The leads from both ends of each capacitor to its supply pin add up to no more than 20 mm.
A second capacitor from pin 1 to pin 8 and from pin 9 to pin 16 is worth considering unless each side's two ground pins are joined close to the package.

operation.text: Each channel carries a logic level across the isolation barrier through an on-chip air-core transformer, with CMOS encode and decode circuits on the two sides; no LED or photodiode is involved. Each side has its own 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply (3.0 V to 5.5 V for the W grades), so a channel can also move a signal between a 3 V side and a 5 V side.

ADuM1400: all four channels run from side 1 to side 2, with one enable (VE2) on side 2 and pin 7 not connected. ADuM1401: channels A, B and C run from side 1 to side 2 and channel D the other way; VE2 enables A to C, VE1 enables D. ADuM1402: A and B run from side 1 to side 2, C and D from side 2 to side 1; VE2 enables A and B, VE1 enables C and D.

A grade (ARW): 1 Mbps, 100 ns propagation delay, 40 ns pulse width distortion. B grade (BRW): 10 Mbps, 50 ns, 3 ns. C grade (CRW): 90 Mbps, 32 ns, 2 ns (maximum delays at 5 V). The automotive WS and WT grades have the A and B data rates, run to 125 °C, and the WT grade's maximum delay at 5 V is 32 ns.

An enable input high or left open turns its outputs on; low sets them to high impedance within 8 ns maximum and back on within 8 ns. The enable pins are best driven to a defined level in a noisy environment.

The logic pins need no external parts. Each supply wants a bypass capacitor of 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF, most easily between pins 1 and 2 for VDD1 and between pins 15 and 16 for VDD2, with no more than 20 mm of total lead length from both capacitor ends to the supply pin. A further capacitor from pin 1 to pin 8 and from pin 9 to pin 16 is worth considering unless each side's two grounds join close to the package. Board coupling across the barrier should be kept small, and whatever coupling remains should reach every pin of one side equally; otherwise fast common-mode transients can push pin-to-pin voltages past the absolute maximum ratings and cause latch-up or damage.

The delay to a low output and the delay to a high output can differ; pulse width distortion is the largest difference between the two and shows how well the input's timing survives. Channel-to-channel matching is the largest delay difference between channels of one part; propagation delay skew is the largest delay difference between separate parts under the same conditions.

Each input edge sends a pulse of about 1 ns through the transformer to a bistable decoder, which it sets or resets. When the input has not changed for about 1 µs, the input side sends refresh pulses carrying the present level, so the output stays correct at DC. If the decoder sees no pulse for about 5 µs, a watchdog takes the input side to be unpowered or failed and sets the output to its default state from the truth table.

With the input side unpowered and the output side powered, an output goes high (enable high or open) or high impedance (enable low), and follows its input again within 1 µs once the input supply returns. With the output side unpowered the output is indeterminate; after that supply returns the output follows the input within 1 µs, or goes to high impedance within 8 ns if the enable is low.

A field can upset a channel only by inducing enough voltage in a receiving coil to set or reset the decoder falsely. Received pulses exceed 1.0 V and the decoder threshold is about 0.5 V, leaving a 0.5 V margin; 3 V operation is the most sensitive case. The allowable field is set so that the induced voltage is at most half that margin. At 1 MHz the limit is 0.2 kgauss, which induces 0.25 V: about half the threshold, so no false transition, and a worst-case hit during a real pulse still leaves 0.75 V against the 0.5 V threshold. That field corresponds to about 0.5 kA flowing 5 mm from the part at 1 MHz. Loops in board traces near strong, fast fields can still pick up enough voltage to trip the logic that follows.

A channel's supply current depends on its supply voltage, its data rate and its output load. The per-channel equations give each input and output channel's current; summing the channels on each side gives IDD1 and IDD2.

Insulation wears out under long voltage stress at a rate set by the waveform. Accelerated life testing at above-rated voltages gives acceleration factors from which time to failure at working voltage is worked out. A bipolar AC voltage is the hardest case and sets the 565 V peak figure for a 50-year life; unipolar AC or DC, which never crosses 0 V, stresses the barrier much less, so the higher approved working voltages hold for 50 years with those waveforms. Any waveform that is neither unipolar AC nor DC is treated as bipolar AC and kept to the 50-year bipolar value. The approved working voltage can exceed the 50-year voltage, and running there can shorten insulation life.

The ADuM1400W, ADuM1401W and ADuM1402W are built under controlled manufacturing for automotive quality and reliability, and some of their specifications differ from the commercial grades (the 125 °C specifications). Only these W models are offered for automotive use.
